parts: Dec. 11, 2025: the Clayton Clipper’s lifting jacks failed on its move to span 3. The rear support fell onto the guideway, and the gantry was out of service for two months. No cause was ever given, but TI Corp. said the wait was for replacement parts.

I wasn’t watching as closely back then, but I think the rear lifting jacks weren’t used again until span 32. Until then, a modified move with a ballast segment took their place. It isn’t shown in this animation.
This support crossing Fraser Highway is different from all the others. It’s a station-style bent: the guideway goes through it instead of over it.
This is the crest of the hill, where the pillars start getting progressively taller.
The design probably had to do with minimizing pillar growth on the 7% grade.
Span 29 crosses the future 72 Ave intersection.
It has 16 segments, more than the 12 the gantry can hang, so crews built it on a temporary support tower.
The animation doesn’t show this.
Span 31 is two big concrete beams. The short support sat right on them, without its blue legs.
A mobile crane moved the rear support across to the end of the double girders on span 43.
Full disclosure: I made up this part.
Not out of thin air, though. It had to work within these limits:
The front support’s beam is too short for the angles, so it has to be the third or fourth support onto the girders.
The gantry can’t tip over. Kind of important.
And the supports have to end up set for a four-support leapfrog that repeats all the way across.
The leapfrog starts here, and I made all of it up.
It takes 14 moves to get the short support onto the hammerhead pillar where spans 47 and 48 meet.
Its blue legs will be waiting there.
The short support is back on its blue legs.
Now the supports spread out again. The rear lifting jacks hold a long support as ballast, while the front lifting jacks carry the short support across span 48.
During the leapfrog, the trolley crane did all the lifting.
Span 50 will have 15 or 16 segments, more than the 12 the gantry can hang, so it will rest on a temporary support tower while they’re hung.
The animation doesn’t show this.
